_README: Published Memphis-area wedding and event vendor pricing, collected by desk research.
THE ONE RULE: every row is a price the vendor publishes on its own public website.
Nothing here is estimated, inferred, averaged from a third-party marketplace, or
remembered. If a vendor does not publish a number, that vendor is not in this file.
A single invented figure would make every other row worthless, because a reader
cannot tell which one was invented.
Each row carries `source_url` (the exact page the price is printed on), `observed`
(the ISO date the page was fetched and read), and `quote` (the vendor's own words,
verbatim, so the figure can be checked against the page without re-deriving it).
scripts/build_wedding_cost_dataset_page.py renders the publication page and the CSV
from this file. scripts/validators/validate_wedding_cost_dataset.py refuses to pass
if any dollar figure on that page does not resolve to a row here or to a derivation
this file defines. That is what stops someone editing a nicer number into the HTML.
Every source_url must also be registered in data/external-sources.json, or
scripts/hostile_review.py will reject the page: this network may only link to URLs
that were actually fetched and returned 200.
title: Memphis Wedding Cost by Guest Count, 2026 Edition

collection_window.method: Every candidate vendor's own website was fetched over HTTP and read as text. A vendor entered the dataset only if a numeric price appeared on a page the vendor controls. Marketplace listings (The Knot, WeddingWire, Zola, Thumbtack, Peerspace, Wedding Spot, Eventective) were used to find candidates and were never used as a price source, because the price shown there is a range the platform assembles rather than the vendor's published rate.

geography: Memphis, Tennessee metropolitan area, including Germantown and Bartlett, TN and the north Mississippi tri-state area vendors serve from Memphis.
not_covered: Alcohol and bar packages. No vendor in this sample publishes a per-person bar price, so the guest-count model below contains no alcohol line at all. This is the single largest gap.
Videography, attire, rings, stationery, hair and makeup, transport, hotel blocks and honeymoon. None were collected.

Actual contracted prices. Everything here is a published list or starting price. What couples pay after customisation, negotiation, peak-date premiums and overtime is not observable from a website and is not claimed.
Tennessee state and local sales tax, service charges and gratuity, except where a vendor publishes them as a line item.

Any claim of a market average. Several categories have one publishing vendor. A category's sample size is printed next to it, and a sample of one is labelled as a sample of one rather than as an average.

Vendors who do not publish prices, which is most of them. That is a selection bias in a knowable direction: vendors who post a starting price are more likely to be competing on transparency or on price, so this sample probably sits below the market it is drawn from.

_why: Guest count is the biggest single cost driver in this category, and it is the one
national wedding sites answer worst: they publish a national average and apply a
city multiplier, which is not a measurement of Memphis.
This derivation uses only per-person and per-item prices from the rows above. It
is arithmetic on published Memphis figures, not a model fitted to anything. Every
input names the row it comes from, so a reader can disagree with an assumption
without having to trust the total.

per_guest_components.label: Catering, one plate
per_guest_components.basis: The Commissary full-service catering, BBQ Shoulder Plate (low) to Rib Plate (high), at the guest-count band the vendor itself publishes.

per_guest_components.label: Non-alcoholic beverage
per_guest_components.basis: The Commissary, iced tea or lemonade (low) to soft drinks (high).

per_guest_components.label: Cake, one serving
per_guest_components.basis: Crave Sweet Shop starting price per serving (low) to Sweet LaLa's starting price per serving (high).

per_guest_components.label: Chair, share of table, and linen
per_guest_components.basis: Affordable Party Rentals. Low: white metal-leg chair $1.75 + 60in round table $9.75 divided by 8 seats + 120in linen $11.50 divided by 8 seats. High: padded banquet chair $3.85 + 72in round table $14.00 divided by 10 seats + 132in linen $15.50 divided by 10 seats.

per_guest_components.label: Service staff
per_guest_components.basis: Off The Square Catering. Low: one server at $15.00 per hour, one server per 25 guests, over a 6-hour reception, gratuity excluded, which is $3.60 per guest. High: the same server line plus one bartender at $18.00 per hour per 50 guests over 6 hours ($2.16 per guest), with the 18% gratuity the vendor publishes applied to both, which is $6.80 per guest. The staffing ratios are this publication's assumption and are stated so a reader can change them; the hourly rates and the gratuity are the vendor's published figures.

fixed_components.label: Photography
fixed_components.basis: Lowest published full-wedding package across the seven photographers in the sample (Shelby Renee Photo, The Glass Slipper) to the highest entry-level figure among them (Elizabeth Hoard Photography's stated range floor).

fixed_components.label: Reception DJ
fixed_components.basis: DJ Mark Anderson's published reception range. SAMPLE OF ONE: this is one Memphis DJ's published range, not a market estimate.

fixed_components.label: Day-of coordination
fixed_components.basis: The Hardin House, Wedding Weekend (day-of) package to the Two Month Planning package. SAMPLE OF ONE.

fixed_components.label: Venue rental
fixed_components.basis: Woodruff-Fontaine House Museum, Carriage House + Garden, to The Kent, Front Street Friday-Saturday. SAMPLE OF TWO venues that publish a rental fee.
fixed_components.capacity_note: The low figure is a venue whose published maximum capacity is 150. At 200 guests it is not an available option, so the low end of the 200-guest total is not achievable at that venue and the venue line would have to be replaced.

national_context.note: The commonly quoted national per-guest range for weddings. It is stated on this page only as a contrast, to make clear that the figures here are a narrower measurement rather than a cheaper city. It is not a Memphis figure and is not part of the dataset.
